chat.lead: The Plan stage starts with an interview:
chat.title: Interview · the worked chat

replies.start: Plan our company's next summer party: 200 employees across five offices in Europe, about €150 each, two wheelchair users, some vegetarians.
replies.reframe: I don’t understand this. Can you explain it with an analogy?
replies.a3: A. Good question, I had forgotten. It was too loud to talk, and people left early.
replies.spec: Turn my answers into a specification.

q1.text: Q1 · Format: one party in one place, or one in each office?
q1.recommended: A, the point is that the offices meet.

q2.text: Q2 · Capacity: do you size the venue for peak concurrent occupancy or for average dwell time?
q2.b: B) Average: about 140, with staggered arrivals
q2.recommended: A, the speeches bring everyone together.

q2Analogy.text: Q2 · Think of booking a restaurant: one long table for everyone at eight, or tables that turn over through the evening?
q2Analogy.a: A) One long table: room for 200 at once
q2Analogy.b: B) Tables that turn over: room for about 140
q2Analogy.recommended: A, everyone sits down for the speeches.

q3.text: Q3 · Like a restaurant review: did last year’s party leave feedback worth reading first?
q3.recommended: A, it shows what to avoid.

why-the-sign-off-is-a-gate.header: Why the sign-off is a gate
why-the-sign-off-is-a-gate.description: Stating every requirement at once is not free: one requirement stated alone was followed 98.7% of the time, but with 19 stated gpt-4o fell to 85.0%, part of it from conflicts between requirements [1]. A short card of essentials is the reason.

yang-what-prompts-dont-say.title: Yang, Shi, Ma, Liu, Kästner, Wu, What Prompts Don't Say: Understanding and Managing Underspecification in LLM Prompts (v3)

a-wrong-early-guess-sticks.description: When instructions were revealed piece by piece, models scored 39% lower on average, mostly as unreliability; they “make assumptions in early turns” and do not recover from a wrong turn [1].

laban-llms-get-lost-in-multi-turn.title: Laban, Hayashi, Zhou, Neville, LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation

focus-beats-volume.description: On a long-memory benchmark, prompts holding only the relevant material, only a few hundred words of relevant material scored significantly higher than full prompts of tens of thousands of words, and even a single distractor lowered results [1].

hong-context-rot.title: Hong, Troynikov, Huber, Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance

plan-then-fresh-session.description: After interviewing for a spec, the vendor's own guidance is to “start a fresh session to execute it”, since the new session “has clean context focused entirely on implementation” [1].

anthropic-claude-code-best-practices.title: Anthropic, Best practices for Claude Code

the-answer-can-be-right-and-the-work-wro.header: The answer can be right and the work wrong
the-answer-can-be-right-and-the-work-wro.description: Among solutions with a correct final answer, the best system cut reasoning errors from 14.0% to 3.4%, so a check on the result alone accepts flawed reasoning [1].

uesato-process-and-outcome-feedback.title: Uesato et al., Solving math word problems with process- and outcome-based feedback

restate.title: The whole task
restate.script: Now let's put the five moves to work on the whole task: plan your company's next summer party, 200 employees across five offices in Europe. This is your first human-in-the-loop agentic workflow: the AI does the work in stages, and you stay in the loop at the points that matter.

interview-and-plan.title: Interview, then plan
interview-and-plan.script: It starts with a plan, and the plan starts with an interview. Before it guesses, the AI asks you questions, one at a time, and one of them is the one you forgot: what went wrong last time. Then it breaks the party down into epics and names the one to start with.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.script: Next, requirements for that one epic. The AI grills you on it in depth, then writes requirements and tickets, and you sign them off before any research starts. If the card is wrong, you want to find out here, while it is cheap.

research-fresh-each-time.title: Research, fresh each time
research-fresh-each-time.script: Now the research. Every ticket gets its own fresh chat, with web search and a source for every number, so no chat drags the whole history along.

one-page.title: One page
one-page.script: Finally, the plan, the requirements and the research are gathered into one page, and that page is your second gate: you sign it off or send it back. A mistake has to get past both gates.

live-next.title: Live next
live-next.script: Same five moves, any task. (pause) Now let's do it live: I will show you how that interview feels when you run it yourself.
